scope: Single frozen public passage, not full repository

claims.name: Lakes are primarily owned by Louisiana State University
claims.description: The Lakes are primarily owned by Louisiana State University, with the exception of City Park Lake and Lake Erie, which are owned by the City-Parish of Baton Rouge.

claims.name: City Park Lake
claims.description: City Park Lake is owned by the City-Parish of Baton Rouge.

claims.name: Lake Erie
claims.description: Lake Erie is owned by the City-Parish of Baton Rouge.

claims.name: Park spaces within the study area are managed by The Recreation and Park Commission for the Parish of East Baton Rouge (BREC).
claims.description: Park spaces within the study area are managed by The Recreation and Park Commission for the Parish of East Baton Rouge (BREC), which is distinct from ownership of the Lakes.
claims.entity: Park spaces within the study area
claims.target: The Recreation and Park Commission for the Parish of East Baton Rouge (BREC)

claims.name: have a strong sense of implied ownership of the Lakes
claims.description: Residents of the neighborhoods that line the study area have a strong sense of implied ownership of the Lakes due to their immediate proximity.
claims.entity: residents of the neighborhoods that line the study area

claims.name: co-opted the lake edges into “private” gardens, reserves, and boat launches
claims.description: Many residents have co-opted the lake edges into “private” gardens, reserves, and boat launches; these additions can create charm and beauty but can also create issues for lake operations, maintenance, and adjacent property owners.

claims.name: residents along the Lakes were engaged and that this sense of ownership is preserved in this Master Plan.
claims.description: The master planning process made every effort to ensure that residents along the Lakes were engaged and that this sense of ownership is preserved in this Master Plan.

claims.name: implied ownership
claims.description: A strong sense of ownership of the Lakes held by nearby residents due to immediate proximity; it is not described as legal ownership.
